goal: A water-resources editor needs to decide whether a three-day station comparison supports an ordered discharge-volume statement. Assess the integrity of the daily records and the volume comparison in parallel. If one researcher sees something that changes how the other should compare the gauges, have them communicate directly while the work is in progress. Decide what the observations and the stated measurement-error scenario actually support. Give a checkable volume difference with units, the observed time span, and any limits on a public conclusion. Preserve a reusable way to repeat this review with fresh observations and make a new decision when the data arrive.

operation.reason: The common-day integration and the range established under the specified error scenario settle the scoped editorial question. The parallel review and fresh decision are saved as a reusable recipe.
unresolved: A probability or confidence level for the difference would require station-specific error evidence beyond the editor’s assumed bounds. The public comparison applies to integrated volume at these two gauges over the three common days. Subdaily ordering and typical or longer-term flow require observations at those time scales.

summary.scope: Volumes integrate over valid simultaneous intervals only. An empty support has zero duration and integrated volume; the mean and ordering there are unknown.

Each station has its own support. Marginal coverage alone does not give simultaneous duration, volumes, or the sign of a paired difference.

modules.focus: Audit the daily station records against the archived USGS original and the prepared record. Verify site and variable/statistic identifiers, qualifiers, native values and units, dates/time support, conversions and error provenance or discrepancies. During the review send the volume analyst a direct peer finding as soon as any source or interval detail affects how to pair, integrate or bound the comparison (including the local daily-mean and approval semantics). Use the research-topic communication mechanism while the volume review is active. Acknowledge consequential findings received.

decisions.rationale: The six approved USGS daily means and their converted rates match row by row. A station-specific aggregation of the prepared record will verify each gauge’s accepted duration and integrated volume against an independent sum in native units. The volume analyst is measuring their joint support and signed bounds.

modules.focus: Evaluate the signed Potomac (01646500) minus Northwest Branch Anacostia (01651000) integrated volume on the common valid support. Independently check the daily-mean integration, sign, time and unit conversions and the editor's stated rate-error scenario. Use the paired method if appropriate. Monitor the shared research topic and engage the Daily-record auditor directly during work about date support, quality flags or how the scenario affects endpoints. Send a comparison-relevant finding or request to the auditor, and apply material peer findings to the calculation.

decisions.rationale: The original USGS series and the daily-record auditor agree on April 1, 2 and 3, 2023 as three complete local days. Each carries an approved daily mean at each site. Multiplying each native rate by 86,400 seconds yields a signed difference of +2,394,360,000 ft³. The prepared record matches the original digest and supplies per-interval litre-per-second rates, flags, and absolute error bounds. The paired calculation will verify the integrated volumes, duration and sign over those dates and furnish versioned readings for a repeat analysis.

modules.focus: Write a reusable, input-parameterized station comparison procedure as a signed GX report for future reviews. Use the original and prepared file schemas as examples. Declare replaceable input roles upstream_original and record, station order and requested local-date window. Specify original-to-prepared audit, validity and duration rules, peer exchange of consequential discrepancies while parallel reviews are open, time and volume units, error provenance, deterministic extrema and independent native-unit arithmetic. Pin discharge-concurrent@1, its no-parameter contract, and the paired.json metrics. Define a fresh lead decision when the new record, audit and volume evidence arrive, including incomplete or zero common coverage, an absent or inapplicable error model, or a zero-crossing interval. Describe a fresh evidence-triggered review, without hardcoding source digests, dates, result values or direction. This is the portable procedure deliverable; no new scientific Job or search is needed.
